Definition: a Pelishtite or inhabitant of Pelesheth
BiblicalUsage: Pelishtiy is a Philistine, an inhabitant of Philistia. They came from Casluhim, and the LORD delivered Israel into their hand for forty years in the days of Samson. David asked who this uncircumcised Philistine was, that he should defy the armies of the living God, and Zephaniah prophesied that the land of the Philistines would be destroyed with no inhabitant.
TheologicalSignificance: I am sure that the Philistines are the picture of every enemy that defies the living God: they are strong, they are near, and they fall. David saw it when he faced Goliath with a sling, and the prophets saw it to the end. I hold that no enemy of God's people outlasts God's patience — the Philistines ruled for forty years and were gone, but Israel remains. The question is never whether the enemy is strong but whether God is with us.
RelatedEvents: David and Goliath; Samson and Delilah
